subject: Zenith Payments: Post-Incident Summary & Action Commitments
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@zenith-pay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Zenith Payments: Post-Incident Summary & Action Commitments

Hi Laura and Raj,

Thank you again for flagging the disruption yesterday. Attached is a concise summary of our findings along with a timeline and immediate mitigation steps we took while the incident was active. High-level summary below: 

- Impact: transient write failures for 11 minutes (12:43–12:54 UTC), affecting approximately 2% of inference requests for your account.
- Root cause: regression in request-routing logic introduced in the autoscaling rollout that caused a small percentage of requests to be misrouted to a drained worker pool.
- Customer impact: failed requests returned 5xx; retries succeeded for most client libraries that used exponential backoff.
- Immediate remediation: reverted the autoscaler config, added a safety check to prevent draining active worker pools, and deployed a hotfix to the routing service.

Attachments sent with this message: zenith_rca_summary_v1.pdf (one-page summary), zenith_timeline_utc.csv (detailed event log), mitigation_plan.xlsx (short-term and medium-term actions).

Next steps we commit to: 
1) Delivery of a permanent autoscaler guardrail (ETA 2027-05-04).
2) A canary rollout and verification window for your production clusters (coordination by Ben).
3) A follow-up technical review with your SRE team next week; proposed slots attached.

Please let me know if anything in the PDF looks off or if you'd like additional data from logs. We appreciate the patience and will prioritize verification on your tenant.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: zenith_rca_summary_v1.pdf, zenith_timeline_utc.csv, mitigation_plan.xlsx

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@zenith-pay.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@zenith-pay.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith Payments: Post-Incident Summary & Action Commitments

Irene, thank you for the quick summary and for the attachments. Quick questions after a read: 

1) Can you confirm how many unique customer API keys observed the failure (approx)?
2) We saw a spike in retries hitting our rate limit; can you confirm whether retries were proxied or surfaced as 5xx from Redwood?
3) For the canary slot, we prefer the afternoon PST window next Wednesday; Raj and I are around 13:00–16:00.

If it helps, we can share an anonymized sample of failed request ids — what log fields would be most useful?

Thanks — appreciate the transparency.

Laura Chen
Head of Ops, Zenith Payments
--
(Attachment: none)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@zenith-pay.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith Payments: Post-Incident Summary & Action Commitments

Laura — quick answers inline: 

1) Unique API keys: ~8 keys from your org saw transient failures (we pulled this from access logs; see column api_key_hash in the attached CSV).
2) Retry behavior: failures surfaced to clients as 5xx; our edge returned a 502 from the misrouted worker. Retries from client SDKs were proxied by Redwood and counted against per-minute token limits — those proxied retries are visible in the timeline CSV as repeated request_ids.
3) Canary: noted your preference; provisionally booking 2027-04-28 13:30–14:30 PST. Ben will send a formal invite when provisioning completes.

Log fields that help: request_id, timestamp_utc, api_key_hash, route, response_code, backend_instance. If you can share request_ids we can correlate immediately.

Ben Carter
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Note: Updated timeline file includes api_key_hash column (redacted) and an explanation row for repeated retries.

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@zenith-pay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@zenith-pay.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T12:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith Payments: Post-Incident Summary & Action Commitments

Thanks Ben — we'll pull 10 sample request_ids and share them via the shared drive link. Two quick asks: 

- Can Redwood confirm whether client retries were billed as normal usage or marked differently for quota/alerting purposes?
- For the permanent guardrail, will there be a changelog entry or release notes we can subscribe to?

We'll upload the sample file to the Drive folder you linked and add a short note with the timeframe.

Laura

--
(Attachment: none)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@zenith-pay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith Payments: Post-Incident Summary & Action Commitments

Laura — Marissa here from Customer Success. Following up on the billing and release notes items: 

- Billing: client retries during the incident were treated as normal traffic for metering. Given the impact we are offering a goodwill usage credit for the affected window; we'll calculate this after correlating request_ids and share a credit estimate by 2027-04-23.
- Release notes / changelog: yes — the permanent autoscaler guardrail will be in the May 4th release notes. We'll provide a scoped changelog entry and an RSS/subscribe link specifically for your tenant.

I'll coordinate the credit calculation with Finance and loop you back with the estimate and documentation. If you'd like a short technical walk-through after the canary, Jonas and I can join the session.

Appreciate your partnership as we close this out.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced previously: mitigation_plan.xlsx (short-term/medium-term tasks).
